issues.t: Automatic transmission hesitates, shifts harshly or fails
issues.sym: The car hesitates or jerks when shifting, bangs into gear, gets stuck in one gear, loses reverse, or whines and stops moving.
issues.why: The 6-speed automatic used in the Sonic has a history of internal failures, and the 2012 model year has by far the most reports. Average failures happen around 70,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid and have the codes read at the first sign of harsh or slipping shifts. If the car will not move or is stuck in one gear, have it towed rather than driven.

issues.t: Transmission turbine shaft can break (recall)
issues.sym: The car may not upshift past second gear, may lose drive and coast, or may only creep along at low speed.
issues.why: On some 2012 Sonics with the 1.8L engine and automatic transmission built from March to June 2012, the transmission turbine shaft could fracture.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Water pump leak on 1.4L turbo
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the front of the engine, the coolant level keeps dropping, you smell sweet coolant, or you hear a rattle or whine from the pump.
issues.why: The water pump on the 1.4L turbo is a known leak point. GM issued special coverage (bulletin 14371) for 2012-2014 Sonics with this engine, extending the pump's coverage to 10 years or 150,000 miles.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and do not let the engine overheat. Ask a Chevrolet dealer whether your car falls under the extended coverage before paying for the repair.

issues.t: Coolant leak from thermostat housing or water outlet
issues.sym: Puddles of coolant, crusty residue around the plastic housing on the engine, a low coolant warning, a sweet smell, or a temperature gauge that runs too high or too low.
issues.why: The thermostat housing and water outlet are made of plastic. Heat cycles make them brittle, so they crack or warp and leak. The thermostat inside can also stick.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant (Dex-Cool) and get the leak fixed soon. Running low on coolant can overheat the engine, especially the 1.4L turbo.

issues.t: PCV valve cover failure causes lean codes and oil burning
issues.sym: Check engine light with lean codes such as P0171 or P0106, a rough or unstable idle, a whistle or hiss from the engine, or the engine using more oil than normal. Early cars can also set code P1101.
issues.why: On the 1.4L turbo the PCV valve is a small rubber diaphragm built into the valve cover. When it tears, it creates a vacuum leak and pulls oil into the intake. On 2012-2013 cars a faulty PCV pipe can also set P1101.
issues.next: Have the codes read. With the engine idling, a strong suction or hiss at the oil filler cap is a common sign. The usual fix is a new valve cover with an updated PCV valve.

issues.t: Turbo wastegate wear causes low boost (P0299)
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0299 (underboost), the car feels weak when accelerating, or there is a rattle from the turbo area at part throttle.
issues.why: Wear at the joint where the wastegate actuator rod connects to the turbo can let the wastegate lose its preload, so the turbo cannot build full boost. GM bulletin PI-1366 covers this on 2013-2015 Sonics.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm the code and inspect the wastegate linkage. Some cars need only an adjustment or clip, while others need a new turbocharger.

issues.t: Timing belt must be replaced on schedule
issues.sym: There is usually no warning. If the belt breaks, the engine stops suddenly and will not restart.
issues.why: The 1.8L engine uses a rubber timing belt rather than a chain. GM's schedule calls for replacement at about 97,500 miles. If it breaks, the engine can be badly damaged.
issues.next: Check your records. If the belt has not been replaced and you are near or past 97,500 miles (or the car is about 10 years old), have it done along with the water pump, which the belt drives.

issues.t: Oil leak from oil cooler housing
issues.sym: Oil drips under the front of the car, oil smoke or a burning smell, or the oil level dropping between changes. In bad cases, oil can show up in the coolant.
issues.why: The 1.4L turbo has an oil cooler mounted on the engine block. Its seals and housing can leak oil, and a failed seal can let oil and coolant mix.
issues.next: Have the leak pinpointed before it gets worse. If the coolant reservoir looks brown or milky, stop driving and have it checked right away, since mixed fluids can damage the engine.

issues.t: Oil pressure switch leaks oil
issues.sym: Oil drips from the side of the engine, sometimes with the oil pressure warning light flickering or coming on.
issues.why: The oil pressure switch screwed into the engine can fail internally and leak oil, or send a false low-pressure warning.
issues.next: Check the oil level right away. If the level is fine and the light stays on, have the oil pressure tested before replacing the switch. The switch itself is inexpensive.

issues.t: Shifter button sticks and car won't come out of Park
issues.sym: The button on the automatic shifter knob sticks, jams or breaks, so you can't move the shifter out of Park or it is hard to shift.
issues.why: The chrome shift knob and its button can crack and bind. GM bulletins PI1086A and PI1086B tell dealers to install a new knob kit rather than a whole shifter.
issues.next: Do not force the lever. Ask a dealer or shop to replace the shift knob kit, which is far cheaper than a new shifter.

issues.t: Front clunk from worn sway bar links or struts
issues.sym: Clunking or rattling from the front end over bumps and rough roads, sometimes with a looser feel in the steering.
issues.why: The front stabilizer (sway bar) links and struts wear out often on the Sonic. TrueDelta also has a report of cracked ball joint housings on an early car.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Sway bar links are a cheap fix; worn struts or ball joints should be replaced in pairs.

issues.t: Fuel gauge sticks or reads wrong
issues.sym: The fuel gauge gets stuck, jumps around, shows full when the tank is low, or shows empty after a fill-up. A fuel level code may appear.
issues.why: The fuel level sender inside the tank wears or its contacts get dirty, so it sends the wrong reading to the gauge. RepairPal lists this as the Sonic's most reported problem.
issues.next: Track your mileage between fill-ups so you don't run out. A shop can test the sender and wiring; usually the sender or fuel pump module is replaced.

issues.t: Radiator cooling fan fails
issues.sym: Check engine light, the temperature gauge climbs in traffic or at idle, or the A/C blows warm when stopped.
issues.why: The electric cooling fan assembly can fail, so the radiator doesn't get enough air at low speed.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge. If it climbs, turn on the heater full blast and pull over safely. Have the fan and its wiring checked before driving in traffic.

issues.t: A/C blows warm air
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only slightly cool air.
issues.why: Owners report failed A/C compressors and other A/C faults, especially on 2013-2014 cars.
issues.next: Have the A/C system checked for leaks and pressures before topping it up. A failed compressor needs replacing along with a system flush.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal sensor fault (P2138)
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P2138, reduced engine power, or the car not responding properly to the gas pedal.
issues.why: Code P2138 means the two signals from the accelerator pedal sensor don't agree. Causes include a bad pedal assembly, the throttle body, or wiring. Some 2012 owners report spending hundreds without a fix.
issues.next: Have a shop check the pedal and throttle body signals and the wiring between them before replacing parts.

issues.t: Battery drain or no-start from corroded ground wire
issues.sym: The car won't crank or start, the battery keeps going dead, or the radio and warning lights act up.
issues.why: A corroded body ground wire can drain the battery and cause no-starts. Weak batteries also cause many electrical complaints on these cars.
issues.next: Have the battery tested and the battery cables and ground wires inspected and cleaned. Replace the battery if it fails the test.

issues.t: Odometer shows dashes instead of mileage
issues.sym: The odometer display shows dashes instead of the mileage reading.
issues.why: Owners of 2013 Sonics report the instrument cluster display losing the mileage reading, which points to a cluster or communication fault.
issues.next: Have the cluster and its connections checked. A software update or cluster repair is usually needed.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not deploy (recalls)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In a crash, the driver's front airbag might not inflate.
issues.why: A shorting bar inside the driver's airbag connector could touch its terminals and block deployment. GM recalled affected cars more than once to fix it.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator may rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. In a crash, the inflator could burst and throw metal pieces.
issues.why: A manufacturing defect could let the driver's airbag inflator rupture when it deploys.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Driver airbag may only partly deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly an airbag warning light. In a severe crash, the driver's airbag may not inflate with full force.
issues.why: A loose electrical connection in the steering column on some cars built in summer 2014 could limit the airbag to its first stage.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Engine block heater cord can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Cracked or worn insulation on the block heater cord, exposing wires.
issues.why: On cars with the optional block heater, the cord insulation can wear or crack, creating a shock risk when it is plugged in.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Fuel tank strap bracket welds may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly a fuel smell or a fuel tank sitting lower than normal.
issues.why: On some cars built in August 2013, the welds on the front fuel tank strap bracket were too weak, so the tank could shift and leak.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Brake lights may flash and cruise control may switch off (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights flash when you are not braking, or cruise control turns off by itself.
issues.why: A fault caused the brake lamps to flash without the brake pedal being pressed and could cancel cruise control.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Burned-out turn signal not shown to driver (recall)
issues.sym: A turn signal bulb is out but the dash indicator still flashes at the normal rate.
issues.why: The body control module did not detect or report a failed turn signal bulb as federal rules require.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Front brake pad may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: Longer stopping distances or a grinding noise when braking.
issues.why: A small number of early 2012 Sonics were built with an inner or outer front brake pad missing.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Windshield washer hose may come off (recall)
issues.sym: The washers stop spraying fluid on the windshield.
issues.why: The washer hose could separate from the fluid reservoir, cutting off washer fluid.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Radio may freeze and silence warning chimes (recall)
issues.sym: The radio screen goes blank and audio cuts out, and warning chimes may not sound.
issues.why: On some 2015 cars the radio could lock up. Since the radio produces safety chimes, those warnings could be lost.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Key and seatbelt warning chimes may not sound (recalls)
issues.sym: No chime when you leave the key in the ignition and open the door, or no seatbelt reminder chime.
issues.why: Radio software could fail to sound required chimes, so the car did not meet federal standards.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.

issues.t: Driver seat-back weld may fail (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash. The driver's seat back could collapse in a rear impact.
issues.why: A weld on the driver's seat-back frame may not have been made correctly on some 2018 cars.
issues.next: Run your VIN through NHTSA or a Chevrolet dealer to see if this recall applies and is still open. The fix is free at any Chevrolet dealer.
